lis.profile: Lis — a cool, deadpan, ironic street narrator of an adult comedy show about used-car flippers. Low calm voice, dry humor, confident.
lis.notes: A standalone adult comedy episode: a tow-truck driver keeps picking up the same broken cars sold by a car flipper. Deadpan ironic narration. Last line — a confident, warm, clear advertising pitch for the bot «Перехват».

zhora.profile: Zhora — a brash, cocky veteran Russian used-car flipper in his 50s, leather jacket, mustache, gold chain; loud, fast, mocking, calls the young rival «студент». Adult street comedy.
zhora.notes: Line 1: over a crackling radio, pleading, fast. Line 2: cheerful, cheeky, short.

vitya.profile: Vitya — a Russian tow-truck driver in his 50s, twenty years on the highway, gravelly tired voice, dry working-class humor. He swears casually and naturally, like ordinary road talk — not shouting, just matter-of-fact. Adult comedy, uncensored.
vitya.notes: Pronounce every swear word fully, clearly and naturally in the flow of speech — never bleep, soften or skip it. Line 1: tired, annoyed sigh. Line 2: matter-of-fact. Line 3: dry joke, deadpan. Line 4: ironic gratitude. Line 5: bored, amazed, slow.

pash.profile: Pashka — a young Russian guy around 22, naive first-time car buyer, nervous and lively.
pash.notes: Line 1: panicked. Line 2: hopeful, naive question. Line 3: proud, happy.
